record.paper_title: Open Questions about Time and Self-reference in Living Systems
record.original_question: What dynamics are necessary and sufficient for a living system to creatively interpret physical memory structures—such as behavioral engrams or genomic sequences—in a way that supports forward-looking goals, especially when memory and self persist through radical bodily or neural remodeling such as metamorphosis or regeneration?

evidence.quote:
The flow of information within this architecture is fascinating and enables behavioral robustness that
we have yet to even begin to emulate in silico [62, 63]. The caterpillar can be trained, and the butterfly
or moth will retain those memories, despite the fact that the brain, the conventional view of the site
of memories, is almost totally destroyed and rebuilt during the metamorphosis process [64], and the
fact that those memories have to be decoded in the context of a totally different body structure and
behavioral repertoire

Crucially in biology, memories (whether behavioral engrams or genomic sequences) must be
interpreted: a dynamic that eventually scales cell-level problem-solving into the advanced intelligence we
observe in brainy animals [65]. The precise dynamics necessary and sufficient for creative interpretation
of physical memory structures in a way that facilitates forward-looking dynamic goals remains very
poorly understood, but it is clear that electrophysiology of all cells, not just of nerves and muscle, is
centrally involved.

artifact.status_search_result: The question concerns the dynamical conditions enabling living systems to creatively reinterpret memory across radical bodily remodeling (metamorphosis, regeneration). It is described in current biological/cognitive-science literature as poorly understood, with no known necessary-and-sufficient mathematical characterization. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.claim: The dynamics necessary and sufficient for creative interpretation of biological memory remain poorly understood and open.
